parts.part: whole town (fortified citadel, ceremonial ground with two 'stadiums', lower town, within an outer fortification)
parts.layout_phase: Period I (Mature Harappan, 'with sub-phases'); the excavator assigns the architecture to Period I but gives no structural phase for the first building of the walls
parts.what_was_built: Shubhra Pramanik's preliminary report on the 2003-04 season of the Archaeological Survey of India describes a roughly rectangular settlement of 410 by 350 m (p. 45) with a rectangular citadel fortification 'built of rubbles and mortar', 7 m high and 4.50 m wide, an outer fortification wall, a gateway with three construction phases, a second gateway leading from the citadel to two 'stadiums', a pillared hall, and an open ground of 200 by 50 m 'in between the citadel and structural remains of the lower town' (pp. 53-54). The deposits are 'Period I-Mature Harappan with sub-phases' and 'Period II-Late Harappan' (p. 47); in the index trench layers 5 to 6A are Mature Harappan and layers 1 to 5 Late Harappan (p. 53). Pramanik places the architecture in Period I: 'As far as the architecture is concerned, it includes fortified citadel, residential houses, systematic drains, pillared halls and stadiums' (p. 55). Below the Mature Harappan layers the lowest 3 m of deposit 'has so far not yielded pottery, etc., excepting for a mud-brick structure of 3m height' (p. 47), a mud-brick platform (STR-5) of 40 courses in two phases (p. 53).
parts.excavator_basis: Cross-dating only, with no calendar range. Pramanik writes that the stadium 'seems coeval with stage IV of Dholavira as the artifacts of Kuran resemble the antiquities from Stages IV and V of Dholavira' (p. 53) and that the Kuran Harappans 'were the migrants from Dholavira in Stage IV' (p. 54). Bisht dates Dholavira Stage IV to c. 2500-2100 BCE (Bisht 2015, p. 104); Pramanik does not quote that range.

syntheses.statement: Rawat summarises the excavations (2003-04 to 2005-06): the town, with a highest mound of about 7 m of Harappan deposit, 'consisted of a citadel, a middle town and a lower town' and yielded 'remains of the Mature and Late Harappan times'; the settlement 'was fortified and furnished with gateways and two enclosures which have been identified as stadiums'.
syntheses.disagreement: Rawat adds a middle town, which Pramanik's 2004 preliminary report does not name; he gives no dates.

parts.conflicts: Whether the lowest 3 m, with its mud-brick platform but no pottery, is Harappan or earlier is left open: 'Whether there was an Early Harappan settlement here or not is a moot point since the lowest 3 m deposit has so far not yielded antiquities' (p. 56). If the platform belongs to the walled layout, the layout phase may predate the Mature Harappan layers of the index trench. The citadel wall was not dated to a phase in the 2003-04 report, and the reports on the 2004-05 and 2005-06 seasons were not available to us.

first_occupation.phase: undetermined: the lowest 3 m of the index trench, aceramic so far except for a mud-brick platform, underlies the Mature Harappan Period I
first_occupation.basis: Pramanik (2004, pp. 47, 56) leaves open whether this deposit is Early Harappan; no dates are given.

sources.citation: Pramanik, S. 2004. Excavation at Juni Kuran 2003-4: A Preliminary Report. Puratattva 34 (2003-04): 45-57. Pages cited are printed page numbers (PDF page minus 10 in the saved scan).
Rawat, Y. S. 2015. Coastal Sites: Possible Port Towns of Harappan time in Gujarat. In S. Keller and M. Pearson (eds), Port Towns of Gujarat, pp. 187-215. Delhi: Primus Books.

notes: Juni Kuran, on the north-eastern edge of Pachchham island in the Great Rann of Kachchh, was excavated by the Archaeological Survey of India from 2003-04 to 2005-06. Only the preliminary report on the first season is available to us. It assigns the fortified citadel, gateways, stadiums and houses to Period I, the Mature Harappan, and cross-dates the stadium to Dholavira Stage IV, so we record Period I as the layout phase with no calendar range. No radiocarbon date, excavator's calendar range or Bayesian model was found. The excavation reports in Indian Archaeology: A Review for 2003-04 to 2005-06 were sought on the ASI Aurangabad circle site (404) and the National Mission on Monuments and Antiquities site (connection timed out). Pramanik's report and Rawat's summary both comment on the site's orientation; per our brief we did not record it.
